subject: Texas AI Docket, Carousel No. 27, September 17th, 2026, Software drafts your lab result note.
body:
Software drafts your lab result note.

Carousel No. 27, September 17th, 2026

Did NOT meet the bar: 6.856 against 8.0. Read before posting.

machine QAPASS, 9 slides, zero fails, zero warns
claimsPASS, 42 verified claims, 5 absences with method, 8 rejected findings
numeralsPASS, 27 numerals over 9 frames, every one reachable from a claim its frame cites
aggregatesPASS, 5 declarations, every one re-derived
deck coherencePASS, mean adjacent jump 8.31 against a 14.9 ceiling, no hard cut
layoutPASS, the rotation holds and the accent is used with restraint
constructionPASS, 4 of 9 frames share the plate primitive, under the 50% line
plan vs renderPASS, 9 of 70 acceptance items machine-checkable and every one holds
verbatimPASS, 9 declared fragments, every one a literal substring of its own claim's quote
locatorsPASS, 8 locators carried by claims, 0 untraced
captionPASS, 148 words, 900 characters, clean against every house rule
sources blockPASS, every claim id the deck prints resolves to a document
sitePASS, house_style, site_fresh, media, seo, schema, schema_contract, port_audit all clean
shipped_checkPASS across every published run
ledgersPASS, topics, artwork and captions agree with their own entries
ownershipPASS, 343 paths all inside the daily lane
completionPASS, the deck shipped on the 5 round cap
scoreSTALE, and the run record says exactly why and by how much
reviewPASS after repair, 8 findings from the review bot on the pull request, every one verified against its source and 8 fixed

What degraded

  • THE DECK SHIPPED UNDER THE BAR. 6.856 against 8.0, a shortfall of 1.144, on the five round cap with zero hard fails standing. That is the one path under the threshold that is not a failure, and it is only that because the run did five rounds of work.
  • Frame 2 is cuttable on FIVE independent judge readings across five rounds. This run chose not to restructure a nine frame deck at round 5 and recorded the disagreement rather than settling it.
  • Frame 3 still reads poorly at feed size after four rounds. Its projection arithmetic now checks to the pixel and two judges still called the monitor a floor lamp. Nothing measures recognisability.
  • Frame 9's halftone reserve was repaired in the source string and never reached the pixels, because lineBoxes reads live geometry and the card is positioned after the canvas work. The deck's one screen still runs under the accent card's type. NOT fixed here, because the deck is past its round cap and this is craft rather than a hard fail. deck_chassis now fails any future deck that does it.
  • Frame 7 omits subsection (f)'s opening trigger clause, which is what makes (f) the health care provision. Two integrity judges disagreed about whether the lowercase opening already marks the cut.
  • Four bleeds declarations disagree with the drawn sheets. layout_check measures the dossier's rect and passes; two craft judges measured the N.sheet call and did not.
  • gov.texas.gov now disallows this crawler across the whole host where the registry records that it serves none. Nothing was fetched from it. The registry is human lane, so the decision is yours.

Named here rather than left out. A run that quietly ships less than it planned teaches nobody anything.

Post this

Upload the PDF to LinkedIn as a document, title it Software drafts your lab result note., paste the post copy under it, then paste the first comment within a minute of posting.

carousel.pdf   contact sheet   the site

1. The post copy

At Memorial Hermann in Houston, software writes the note before the clinician does.

The assistant is built into Epic and drafts the note a patient gets with a lab result. The clinician can review and edit it.

The system reports 32% fewer follow-up messages when clinicians started from the draft, and an average of nine seconds saved per result comment. healthsystemCIO wrote on September 10th that the figures come from Epic and its customer, and that the 32% counts clinicians who chose it.

Section 552.051 took effect January 1st. Subsection (b) puts its disclosure duty on a governmental agency. Subsection (f) puts it on the provider of the service or treatment. Chapter 552 has no section headed Applicability.

Nine slides go from the announcement to the statute. Ask who wrote the note, before a first visit.

Does subsection (f) reach a hospital that is not an agency?

#Houston #HB149 #MemorialHermann

2. The first comment

The machine changed itself

  • bleed_witness.py, a new gate that reads every drawn box out of each slide's own script.
    layout_check measured the dossier's declared bleeds against the dossier's declared rect, so it was asking the declaration whether the declaration was true. Four frames of nine declare a bleed none of them draws. Over all 27 shipped decks the first cut invented three failures, because the engine draws scenes in metres, so three structural guards followed.
  • deck_chassis gains a fifth rule. Nothing a TXDECK.lineBoxes call reserves may be repositioned after it.
    One finding across 27 decks and 240 frames, and it is frame 9 of this one. The card was added to the reserve selector, reported fixed, and positioned twenty lines after the call that measures it.
  • ledger_check --derive now writes the derivation it already judged.
    Proved against the 2026-08-25 corruption, byte-stable on a ledger that was already right, and asserted unable to clear a freehand-move-name finding.
  • Refused, and written to the backlog instead. Nothing measures whether a drawn object is recognisable.
    Frame 3 checks to the pixel at five measurements and two judges still called the monitor a floor lamp. All three gate designs considered were taste with a number bolted on, and the improvement actually available is upstream in an agent definition under .claude/, which no unattended run can write.

Every change is logged in ledger/carousel/upgrades.json.

Notes

Prompt audit, the reading that counts, taken after the upgrade worker and the commits. 1,673 tool calls measured and none waited on a human. THE DECK SHIPPED UNDER THE BAR ON THE FIVE ROUND CAP, 6.856 against 8.0. The rubric's cap ends the search and does not lower the standard, and no hard fail was standing at the end. Two were found and cleared during the rounds, both on the statute frames. A REVIEW BOT FOUND EIGHT THINGS ON THE PULL REQUEST AND ALL EIGHT WERE REAL. Every one was the same shape, a claim the copy made that its own evidence did not carry. A source's optional "can" published as a guarantee, a "Nothing is deployed" the abstract never said, a $20 million whose only trace was the source URL slug, the statute's definition of health care services slid one noun over into a definition of the provider it never defines, three statutory clauses the text-only article was publishing with their duty holders dropped as furniture, subsection (f)'s emergency carve-out missing from frame 9's deadline, the caption's dropped "average", and an award record whose awardee and principal investigator the summary asserted with no quote under either. All eight repaired past the round cap, because the cap governs the design loop and not truthfulness. CHECKING THOSE FINDINGS FOUND A WORSE ONE THE BOT DID NOT SEE. Two NSF claims carried verbatim quote strings that are not in the source at all. One invented backslash escaping and welded two fields that sit about 1,300 characters apart, and one swapped the source's curly apostrophe for a straight one. Nothing caught them, because no gate tests a claim's quote for literal containment in the document it names. verbatim_check proves the slide's fragments against the claim's quote, one link further down, and takes the quote itself on trust. That gate is the next run's first work, ahead of everything else in the record. CI caught the email payload before main did, on email_check --all, which is the carousel no. 7 failure exactly. It cost one push rather than a red main and a second pull request. THIS BRANCH IS PUSHED BY SOMETHING THAT IS NOT THIS SESSION, and it is recorded as a measurement with no explanation attached. push.sh reported cannot lock ref with the commit already on the remote, as documented. Then the remote was found carrying a second commit no push had been issued for, and then the final commit was never pushed by any command this session ran and was the branch head within two minutes, with CI already running against it. The consequence is the ordering rather than the mystery. The routine commits, runs its gates, and pushes when the verdict is green, so a commit that reaches the remote on its own starts CI against work the local suite has not finished judging. Harmless here, because the verdict came back green on cb477dcabc39 at 142 steps passed and CI was green on the same SHA. On a run whose gates go red it would mean the red work was already public.

This is a draft. Nothing was sent. The deck is already merged to main, so these links are live. Posting is the only step left, and it is yours.
